Lesson 2 · Business route

Read patterns without overclaiming

What budget covers a useful share of lodging offers?

Fictional case. The observations are generated for teaching, not evidence about a real business. The full data-generating process is in the technical appendix.

What the data show

Among 360 fictional prices, the sample mean is 123.73 CU and the median is 119.08 CU. The difference points to a right tail: a single typical-price number hides some costly offers.

What would you decide?

Show a distribution and the share below the proposed budget for each town. State the denominator. Do not turn a descriptive association into a claim that changing town causes a price change.

Pause and explain

Would the overall mean alone be enough to set a travel budget?

Compare your reasoning

No. The tail, the proportion under the budget and the mix of towns matter to the decision.

What the generator knows

Reveal the known truth after making your judgment

The script specifies how these fictional prices and group labels are drawn. The displayed mean and median are realized sample summaries, not population constants or real-market estimates.

The truth belongs to this invented model. A real organization would still need to test the assumptions and collect its own evidence.
